component.name: Chip
component.description: Pill-shaped filter toggle. Each chip is an independent toggle button (aria-pressed); the page owns which chips are pressed. Default: neutral border and subtle text. Pressed: brand border and brand text. Pure filter indicator — not a navigation element. Label-only; no dropdown arrow.

when: Filtering a list or carousel by category (e.g. All Courses, Design, Development)
Multi-select filtering: each chip toggles one filter on or off independently
Showing current filter state visually — a pressed chip reads as brand-colored

patterns.name: filter-bar
patterns.description: A labelled group of Chips for multi-select filtering: each chip toggles its filter independently, and the page holds the set of active filters. The row is a role=group named by the section heading or an aria-label.
patterns.tree: Inline(gap=sm, wrap=true, role=group, aria-labelledby=<heading id>) > [Chip(pressed=true), Chip(pressed=true), Chip, Chip]

patterns.name: filter-bar-single
patterns.description: The same labelled group used as a single-select filter: the page keeps one active value and presses exactly one chip (Homepage 'Discover new courses'). Chip itself is unchanged; exclusivity is page logic.
patterns.tree: Inline(gap=sm, wrap=true, role=group, aria-labelledby=<heading id>) > [Chip(pressed=true), Chip, Chip, Chip]

antiPatterns.scenario: Using Chip for navigation that changes the URL
antiPatterns.reason: Chip renders a <button> — links that produce a URL change should be <a> elements.
antiPatterns.alternative: Use an anchor tag or a Tab component if routing is needed.

antiPatterns.scenario: Using Chip for a primary call-to-action
antiPatterns.reason: Chips signal filter/selection; they carry no action weight.
antiPatterns.alternative: Use Button for actions (submit, save, download).

antiPatterns.scenario: Using Chip with a dropdown arrow
antiPatterns.reason: The dropdown variant is out of scope; the page uses label-only chips.
antiPatterns.alternative: Compose a Select or a custom popover for dropdown filtering.

antiPatterns.scenario: Placing a Chip alongside a Button in the same Inline row as interactive siblings
antiPatterns.reason: Chip is a selection toggle (state); Button is an action trigger (event). Mixing them in the same row conflates filtering with acting and confuses interaction semantics.
antiPatterns.alternative: Group Chips in their own Inline filter bar. Place action Buttons in a separate row. Never use Chip as a substitute for a Button or vice versa.

antiPatterns.scenario: A row of Chips without a group name
antiPatterns.reason: Screen readers announce each chip as 'toggle button, pressed' with no indication of what the chips filter or that they belong together.
antiPatterns.alternative: Give the Inline role=group and aria-labelledby pointing at the nearest heading (or an aria-label).

purpose.false: Resting state. Transparent background, subtle text, default border.
purpose.true: Active selection. Brand border and brand text to signal the active filter.

states.description: Transparent background, subtle text, default border.
Adds neutral-subtlest background; border and text unchanged.

Momentary press feedback (CSS :active) in both pressed and unpressed chips: overlay.active background, text one step darker (text.default unpressed, text.interactive.hover pressed) to hold AA on the stronger overlay. Orthogonal to the pressed prop.
Persistent toggle-on (aria-pressed=true): brand border and brand text; set via the pressed prop. Not the momentary press — that is the active state.
Muted text and border; pointer-events blocked natively.

ariaAttributes: aria-pressed — reflects the pressed prop so screen readers announce the toggle state

keyboardInteractions.action: Fires onClick, then onPressedChange(!pressed) (caller controls state)
Moves focus to the next focusable element

accessibility.notes: Uses a native <button> element with aria-pressed. Controlled only: the caller owns pressed (filter state always drives page content) and groups chips in a container with role=group and an accessible name (see the filter-bar patterns).
